results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response:
The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. The mushroom body lobe system consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, which have different structures at different life stages. The lobes are further divided into compartments such as α, β, γ1, γ2, and γ4.

results.title: Neuron type classification
results.question: What types of Kenyon cells exist in the adult Drosophila brain?
results.response:
There are several types of Kenyon cells in the adult Drosophila brain. The main subtypes include alpha/beta, alpha'/beta', and gamma Kenyon cells, which can be further subdivided into different classes. VFB's ontology places 7 direct subtypes under [Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003686 "Open Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), including [adult Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049825 "Open adult Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [alpha'/beta' Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100249 "Open alpha'/beta' Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [gamma Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00100247 "Open gamma Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [immature Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047995 "Open immature Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [larval Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00049826 "Open larval Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), [multi-claw Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047994 "Open multi-claw Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [single-claw Kenyon cell](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047993 "Open single-claw Kenyon cell in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB holds [37](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003686,SubclassesOf "Run in VFB: Subclasses of Kenyon cell") subclasses of Kenyon cell.

results.title: Basic connectivity
results.question: What are the main input neurons to the mushroom body?
results.response: The main input neurons to the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are sensory interneuron afferents to the calyx. VFB records show [366](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPresynapticHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body") neurons with presynaptic terminals in mushroom body, including larval uniglomerular projection neurons and larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neurons.

results.title: Neuroanatomy
results.question: What brain regions does the antennal lobe connect to?
results.response: The [antennal lobe](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003924 "Open antennal lobe in Virtual Fly Brain") connects to various brain regions through neurons with presynaptic and postsynaptic terminals. Neurons with presynaptic terminals in the antennal lobe include [larval antennal lobe picky local neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111694 "Open larval antennal lobe picky local neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [larval antennal lobe broad local neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111700 "Open larval antennal lobe broad local neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and adult olfactory receptor neurons. Neurons with postsynaptic terminals in the antennal lobe include adult antennal lobe projection neurons, such as DL5, DM4, VA1d, VL1, VL2a, VM2, and VM4, as well as multiglomerular antennal lobe projection neurons like L1 adPN.

results.title: Cell count
results.question: Approximately how many neurons are in the adult Drosophila central brain?
results.response:
The [adult central brain](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047887 "Open adult central brain in Virtual Fly Brain") contains approximately 32,388 neurons, according to FlyWire reports.

**Published neuron-count estimates — adult central brain** (from the literature):

- ~32,388 neurons (Whole adult brain, both optic lobes and ocellar ganglia included. Ventral nerve cord NOT included; neurons crossing the neck connective are truncated at the brain boundary. Subcount: fully in central brain. One female adult. Dataset: FlyWire connectome neurons, v783.) — [Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Nature 634(8032):124-138 — PMID 39358518](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07558-y "Open Dorkenwald S et al. (2024) Nature 634(8032):124-138 — PMID 39358518 via DOI (new tab)")

_FlyWire reports 32,388 neurons FULLY CONTAINED in the central brain out of 139,255 in the whole brain. Neurons that arborise in the central brain but also elsewhere are not in that subcount, so it is a lower bound on 'neurons in the central brain', not a census of them._

_VFB has annotated 9,413 neuron types with some part in adult central brain — a curated annotation count, not the biological total._

Reference: [How many neurons are in the fly brain?](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/docs/concepts/neuron-counts/ "Open “How many neurons are in the fly brain?” — Virtual Fly Brain documentation (new tab)")

results.title: Central complex structure
results.question: What are the main components of the Drosophila central complex and what functions are they associated with?
results.response: The main components of the Drosophila central complex include the ellipsoid body, the fan-shaped body, the three paired noduli, the asymmetrical bodies, and the protocerebral bridge. These components are associated with functions such as navigation and orientation, locomotor control, and sleep/arousal and memory-related behaviours. The answer uses the reading "[adult central complex](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00003632 "Open adult central complex in Virtual Fly Brain")", but VFB also holds information under alternative names including anterior chiasma of the central complex, posterior chiasma of the central complex, central complex neuroblast, and [adult central complex on adult brain template JFRC2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFB_00030866 "Open adult central complex on adult brain template JFRC2 in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB holds [363](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in adult central complex") records of neurons with some part in adult central complex and [362](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00003632,NeuronsSynaptic "Run in VFB: Neurons with synaptic terminals in adult central complex") records of neurons with synaptic terminals in adult central complex.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. It has a distinct anatomy and connectivity, with a large descending axon that is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. The axon enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side. The giant fiber neuron has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget.

The giant fiber neuron connects to several downstream classes, including [mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00053153 "Open mesothoracic extracoxal trochanter depressor muscle motor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult efferent neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051964 "Open adult efferent neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [NB3-3 lineage primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00048874 "Open NB3-3 lineage primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult IN18B034 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20010307 "Open adult IN18B034 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [peripherally synapsing interneuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00007408 "Open peripherally synapsing interneuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult premotor neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00051437 "Open adult premotor neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [Notch ON hemilineage primary neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047106 "Open Notch ON hemilineage primary neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult IN06B008 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20009235 "Open adult IN06B008 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"). results.question: Based on connectivity data, what neuron types might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body? Could visual information reach the memory circuit?

The connectome data indicates that there is a plausible multi-step pathway between the visual system and the [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain"). VFB records show that adult visual projection neurons have presynaptic terminals in the mushroom body.

The strongest specific targets of [visual system neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00047736 "Open visual system neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), ranked by mean synaptic weight per connected pair, include [adult posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum neuron 061](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20002119 "Open adult posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum neuron 061 in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum neuron 106](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20002164 "Open adult posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum neuron 106 in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult vest neuron 049](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20003515 "Open adult vest neuron 049 in Virtual Fly Brain"). The strongest specific inputs to visual system neuron, ranked by mean synaptic weight per connected pair, include [adult CB0574 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20004319 "Open adult CB0574 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), [adult CB0677 neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20004409 "Open adult CB0677 neuron in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [adult posterior slope neuron 083](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_20001838 "Open adult posterior slope neuron 083 in Virtual Fly Brain").

Some neuron types that might mediate a connection between the visual system and the mushroom body include [adult odd neuron of the calyx](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111628 "Open adult odd neuron of the calyx in Virtual Fly Brain"), [larval uniglomerular projection neuron 63a](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111675 "Open larval uniglomerular projection neuron 63a in Virtual Fly Brain"), and [larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neuron C2](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00111716 "Open larval antennal lobe multiglomerular projection neuron C2 in Virtual Fly Brain"). results.question: What is the connectivity between thermosensory neurons and the mushroom body? Could temperature information influence memory formation?
